intro: Work out what participants see and are asked to donate from this platform: load a test package, decide what happens to each part of it, and check the preview.
exportsIntro: Data donation packages used only to work out the tree for this platform: your own (the zip or folder you downloaded from the platform) or a synthetic example. They stay in this browser tab: nothing is stored or sent, and closing the tab removes them. Only the tree and your decisions are saved, without any values. You can add several, for example in different languages; their structure is combined.
filesIntro: Save this platform's tree as structure.json and importer.json, or open files saved earlier or shared by another project.
confirmStartOver: This clears all decisions, names and matches for this platform. The structures you have seen stay. Have you saved your files? Continue?
started: Here is the structure of your package, with a table for every list. Everything starts undecided: participants don't see it until you choose to show it or ask them to donate it (you can change that in Platform settings).
opened_one: Opened. {{count}} configured part is not in any structure seen so far.
opened_other: Opened. {{count}} configured parts are not in any structure seen so far.
openFailed: These files could not be opened: {{reason}}
pending_one: {{count}} configured part is not in any structure seen so far. It is kept and saved, and applies once a package has it.
pending_other: {{count}} configured parts are not in any structure seen so far. They are kept and saved, and apply once a package has them.
onlyUndecided: Only show what is still undecided
descriptionHelp: One sentence, used when we ask for this field, for example “the time you watched each video”.
raw: Donate the value as it is in the file, not converted
previewIntro: Exactly what one participant would see with your current decisions. A participant uploads one package, so this shows one at a time: by default the structure, with a placeholder for each value.
previewEmpty: Add a test package to see the preview.
noTables: With these decisions, participants would see nothing yet. Set fields to Show or Donate under Decisions, or let participants see undecided parts in Platform settings.
noTablesInPackage: This package has nothing for the tables participants would see, so a participant with it would see no tables.
keysHelp: Are the keys here data rather than names of fields, such as the people who replied or the days of a diary? Then each key becomes a row, with the key and its value as columns.
keysAreData: The keys here are data: each key is a row of a table with a key and a value column.
keysDecisionHelp: The decision here is about the keys themselves, such as the names of the people who replied.
confirmKeys: All keys here become one position, and their names are not kept, because they are data. Decisions that differ between them are listed afterwards. Continue?
recordTable: Fields that are not part of a list

viewHelp.fields: Only tables and the fields in them, named as their columns. Hover a field to see where it is in the file.
viewHelp.tree: Everything in the files, including the folders, objects and HTML in between.

chartIntro: Count rows over time or per value, from the packages you loaded. This runs in your browser; it is a first step towards views participants can make themselves.
readAsHelp: How the value is read. Participants see, and donate, the value as read here.
cleanHelp: Cleaning steps, applied in order before the value is read.
filterHelp: Rows must meet every condition here. Use it to leave out rows that are not the participant's own activity, such as ads.
filterExclude: Leave out the rows that meet this instead
suggestIntro: These parts are new, and sit where a part you already have is missing. They may be the same thing, renamed or translated. Combine them into one row to give them the same settings, or give them the same name to keep their own settings and show them to participants as one.
required: Required: an upload only fits when this is there
requiredHelp: Any of its matches counts. Use it for parts every package has; a participant without them cannot add their data.
newChildrenAsk: Read, show and ask about them
newChildrenHelp: Skipped parts are never opened, shown or offered for structure sharing. That keeps uploads small and the questions short, but you will not hear about renamed or new parts here.
findTitle: Finding the package in a bigger upload
findHelp: Participants pick their package as a zip, a folder or a file, and that is tried first, without looking at its name. If it does not fit, Combray looks inside it for files or folders with one of these names, such as Takeout or watch-history*.json. Use * as a wildcard; letters can be upper or lower case.

problem.too-many-files: This upload has more files than Combray looks through. Pick the package itself.
problem.too-big: This upload is larger than Combray reads in a browser.

handoffFailed: Signing in did not finish (the link from the key page was used or expired). Please sign in again.
noProjects: No projects yet. Create one below, or ask a colleague to add you to theirs.
projectNoAccess: waiting for access to the encryption key
keysElsewhere: Opening donations, creating project encryption keys and publishing happen on the key page, with your passkey.
signInTitle: Sign in to the researcher workspace
signInIntro: You sign in with your passkey, on the key page: a small, separate page that holds the encryption keys of your projects. You come straight back here afterwards, and stay signed in while you work (until you have been away for an hour, and at most for a working day).
projectNotFound: This project is not one of yours

project.notPublished: Not published yet: participants cannot open this project.
project.unpublished: Your latest changes are not visible to participants until you publish them.
project.detailsIntro: What participants see, and who can take part. Participants open this project at /p/{{id}}/.
project.name: Name
project.descriptionHelp: A short introduction participants see when they open the project.

modes.optional: Optional: use an id from the link when there is one
modes.required: Required: only participants with an id from their link

project.patternHelp: A regular expression the whole id must match, such as P[0-9]{4}. Never shown to participants.
project.saveFailed: Saving did not work. Please try again.
project.nameRequired: Give the project a name, in English or Dutch.
project.detailsInvalid: Something here is not accepted. Check the names and the id pattern (no repeated groups such as (a+)+).
project.platformsIntro: The platforms participants can add data from. Per platform, you decide which parts participants see and which they are asked to donate.
project.confirmRemovePlatform: Remove this platform and its decisions from the draft? Participants keep seeing it until you publish.
project.platformFailed: This platform could not be loaded.

save.failed: Not saved. Check your connection; your changes are kept here for now.

project.waitingForAccess: waiting for a colleague to give access
project.noKeyYet: has not set up a passkey yet
project.researchersHelp: Adding colleagues and giving them access to the encryption key happen on the key page, after comparing a short code. Add a trusted backup researcher: someone who can give you access to the encryption key again if you ever lose both your passkey and your recovery code.
project.donationsFailed: The donations could not be loaded.
project.donationsHelp: Donations are encrypted: open them on the key page with your passkey. Per platform counts come next.
project.noAccess: You can work on this project, but not open its donations or publish it yet: a colleague needs to give you access to its encryption key. Read them your key code from the key page when they ask.

steps.title: Set up this project
steps.encryptionKeyHelp: Participants’ donations are locked with it, and only researchers with access to it can open them. Participants cannot donate until it exists.
steps.encryptionKeyAction: Create it on the key page
steps.platformsHelp: The platforms participants can share data from, and per platform what they see and are asked to donate.
steps.consentHelp: What participants read about the study, and the statements they agree to before they share their data.
steps.publishHelp: Participants can open the project once it is published. Publishing happens on the key page, with your passkey, because it changes what participants see and are asked to donate.

consent.intro: What participants read about the study, and agree to, before they share their data. They see it on the page where they review and share what you ask for. Changes reach participants when you publish.
consent.informationHelp: Who you are, why you do this study, what you ask for and what you do with it, how long you keep it, that taking part is voluntary and how to withdraw, and whom to contact with questions or complaints. Plain text; an empty line starts a new paragraph. Your ethics committee may ask for specific wording.
consent.statementsHelp: Statements participants tick, every one, before they can share, such as "I have read the information about this study" or "I am 16 or older". The donation records the statements as the participant saw them.
consent.always: Participants always also confirm that they have looked at what will be shared, and see how their donation is encrypted and how to withdraw it.
consent.invalid: This could not be saved: a statement is empty in both languages, or a text is too long.

newProject.title: New project
newProject.name: Name
newProject.idHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Participants open the project at {{path}}; it cannot be changed later.
newProject.taken: A project with this address exists. Choose another.
newProject.invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes only.

values.title: Values in your test packages
values.noPackages: Load a test package to see what this field holds.
values.notFound: This field is not in the test packages you loaded.

signInFirstTime: First time? The key page emails you a code, once, to confirm your address, and helps you set up your passkey and recovery code.
noKeyPage: This server has no key page set up, so researchers cannot sign in. Ask the server operator.

tabs.label: Tree editor
tabs.needsPackage: This needs a tree to work on. Load a test package first, your own or one of the examples.

learn.title: Learn how the studio works
learn.linkHelp: Try the tree editor with example data first. No account or passkey needed.
learn.intro: This is a place to practise. In a project you do the same thing for each platform you ask participants about: you work out what they will see, and what you will ask them to donate. Here you can try it with an example package, without a project.

steps.packages: Test packages: load an example, or a data download package of your own. Its structure becomes a tree.
steps.decisions: Decisions: for each part of the tree, choose whether participants see it, are asked to donate it, or whether it is ignored.
steps.preview: View as participant: see the tables a participant would get from this package.
steps.chart: Charts: try how the data can be counted and shown, as participants will explore it.

learn.privacy: Packages stay in this browser tab and are gone when you close it. The tree and your decisions (never any values) are kept in this browser, so you can come back to them.
learn.noServer: This server has no researcher accounts, so only this practice workspace is available here.

undecidedShown: Participants see parts you have not decided on
undecidedShownHelp: Off: participants see only what you set to show or donate. On: they also see what is still undecided, including parts that are new since you last looked. Either way, participants can switch to "Raw data" to see their whole package as it is.
tableHelp: The entries of this become the rows of a table, and this label is the table's name.

dataStatus.structureOnlyHelp: No test package is loaded in this tab, so you are working with the tree alone: names and types, no values. Values of fields and charts need a test package.
dataStatus.keptHelp: Values from {{names}}, kept with the project.
dataStatus.temporaryHelp: Values from {{names}}, loaded in this tab only: closing or reloading it drops them.

structurePreview: The tables and columns participants would get, with placeholders: choose a test package above to see real values.
sameStructure: This package has the same structure as {{name}}, so it adds nothing to the tree. Its values are available too.
headerRow: The first row holds the column names
headerRowHelp: For a table whose header is written as an ordinary row, so its columns only have names like #cell[0]. Participants then see the first row's text as the column names, and not as a row. Only how the table is shown changes: the data, and what participants donate, keep the row as it is. Columns you gave a label keep your label.

kept.addIntro: A data download package of your own (the zip or folder you got from the platform) or a synthetic example. Its structure is kept with this platform, so the tree knows it and everyone in the project sees it. Its values stay in this tab, unless you keep them too.
kept.keepValues: Keep its values with the project
kept.keepValuesHelp: Tick this only for a package that is synthetic or holds nothing sensitive, such as one from a test account you made. Its values are then stored on the server with this project, readable by everyone in the project after signing in, so you can see them without uploading the package again. You confirm that this is fine by ticking the box.
kept.title: Kept with this platform
kept.none: No test packages kept yet. Packages you add keep their structure here.
kept.loadFailed: The kept values could not be loaded. The tree is fine; try again later.
kept.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}} from this platform, for everyone in the project? Its structure stays in the tree.
kept.temporaryIntro: Their values are shown here until you close or reload this tab.
kept.temporaryHelp: Load a package to see its values here, in this tab only: nothing of its values is stored. Its structure is kept with the platform, like that of every test package, so new parts show up in the tree.
kept.savedWithValues: It is kept with this platform, values included.
kept.savedStructure: Its structure is kept with this platform.
kept.saveFailed: It could not be kept with the platform; it is loaded in this tab only.
kept.too_big: It is too big to keep its values (at most 25 MB); it is loaded in this tab only.
kept.too_many: This platform already keeps the values of 10 packages; remove one first. This one is loaded in this tab only.
kept.temporaryHelpPractice: Load a package to see its values here, in this tab only: nothing is stored anywhere.

conflict_one: two keys side by side in {{count}} package
conflict_other: two keys side by side in {{count}} packages
conflictHelp: This row matches two different keys that are next to each other in one package, so it is not clear which value is meant. Make its matches narrower, or split it into one row per key.
nameMismatchHelp: Rows with this name have different decisions. Each row keeps its own decision for its own data, which is allowed but unusual: participants see one column with a mix.

name.title: Name
name.help: The name participants see for this part, instead of its key in the file. Rows with the same name are one table or column for participants; each row keeps its own settings.
name.badgeHelp: This row’s name. Rows with the same name are one table or column for participants.
name.useExisting: Or use a name you already have
name.shared_one: {{count}} other row has this name: changing it changes it there too.
name.shared_other: {{count}} other rows have this name: changing it changes it there too.
name.remove: Take the name off this row

match.title: Matches
match.help: The keys in the files this row stands for: exact keys, or regular expressions. A row with several matches takes the data of each, with the same settings, for example a file and its translation.
match.virtual: This part is not configured yet: it matches its own key. Adding a match makes it a configured row.
match.new: Another key, or a regular expression
match.shared: The same data is also in {{names}}: every row that matches a key gets its data.
match.confirmLast: {{match}} is this row’s last match: removing it removes the row and its settings. Continue?

combine.title: Combine with another row
combine.help: Combine rows that are the same thing under different keys, such as a file and its translation, into one row with all their matches and one set of settings. To keep their own settings, give them the same name instead.
combine.together_one: Not combined: both are in {{count}} package, side by side, so they hold different data. Give them the same name instead if participants should see them as one.
combine.together_other: Not combined: both are in {{count}} packages, side by side, so they hold different data. Give them the same name instead if participants should see them as one.
combine.done_one: Combined. {{count}} setting differed: the first row’s is kept.
combine.done_other: Combined. {{count}} settings differed: the first row’s are kept.

sameName.help: Keep the rows and their settings, and show them to participants as one table or column.

select.label: Selected rows
select.help: Tick rows to combine them into one, or to give them the same name.

badRegex: That is not a valid regular expression.
